summary: The code has severe implementation issues: the Simulation.run method is effectively empty (only a stray docstring), the main() function does nothing, and the required metrics and validation criteria are not computed. Additionally, the global main() call appears to be embedded inside the run docstring and thus will not execute. While most classes and interactions are sketched, the simulation loop and outputs are missing, and several specification metrics are unimplemented.

issues.description: Simulation.run is not implemented; it contains only a docstring and no execution logic or return value.
issues.solution: Implement the run() method to iterate over the configured time horizon (e.g., for day in range(self.time_horizon_days): self.step(day)), compute and return the specified metrics and validation results.

issues.description: main() is defined but does nothing; the code never instantiates Simulation or runs it.
issues.location: function main() at top of file
issues.solution: Implement main() to parse parameters (or load defaults), construct Simulation(params), call sim.run(), and output results (e.g., print JSON).

issues.description: The global main() call appears to be inside the unclosed run() docstring, so it will not execute.
issues.location: Module bottom near the end of Simulation.run docstring
issues.solution: Close the run() docstring properly and ensure the line 'main()' is at module scope (not inside any docstring or block).

issues.description: Required metrics are not computed: time_to_target_adoption, peak_adoption_level, sustained_adoption_level, adoption_inequality_index, policy_effect_size, mask_shortage_incidents (naming mismatch).
issues.solution: Track and compute these metrics. For example: compute peak and sustained adoption from adoption_rate_over_time; compute time to target (e.g., first day adoption >= 0.7); compute inequality index across specified groups; run a counterfactual without mandate to estimate policy_effect_size; rename 'shortage_incidents' to 'mask_shortage_incidents'.

issues.description: Validation criteria are not assessed: convergence_of_adoption, target_adoption_threshold, no_inventory_negatives.
issues.location: Simulation.run() end or separate validation function
issues.solution: After the simulation, check: (1) 7-day rolling change < 0.005 for convergence; (2) adoption >= 0.7 within time horizon under mandate-on; (3) assert retailer inventories never go negative. Return validation flags.

issues.description: Policy effect size requires a counterfactual scenario (mandate off) but code only runs a single scenario.
issues.solution: Run the simulation twice: with mandate per parameters and with mandate_off (or mandate_start_day beyond horizon), and compute the difference in adoption trajectories or peak/sustained levels to derive policy_effect_size.

issues.description: The retail shortage metric increments if any single purchase attempt faces shortage, not strictly when aggregate demand exceeds inventory as specified.
issues.solution: Aggregate total requested quantity versus available inventory per time step and count a shortage incident when total demand > inventory.

issues.description: Parameter fields risk_signal_amplitude and risk_signal_decay are not used to evolve risk over time; price_elasticity_of_demand is unused.
issues.solution: Evolve a risk signal over time (e.g., exponentially decaying with amplitude) and incorporate it into individuals' risk perceptions. Use price elasticity in purchase decision or retailer price adjustment to affect demand.

issues.description: Naming mismatch with specification: metric name should be 'mask_shortage_incidents', but code tracks 'shortage_incidents'.
issues.solution: Rename key to 'mask_shortage_incidents' and ensure it is returned.

issues.description: Location.broadcast_signage() is defined but not used; a hardcoded +0.02 signage boost is applied instead.
issues.solution: Use broadcast_signage() from visited or public locations to inform the observed_public_wearing boost.

issues.description: A large number of 'home' and 'work/school' locations are created (O(population)), which may be heavy but still manageable for 5k population.
issues.solution: If needed, reduce the number of explicit home locations or avoid simulating enforcement at home; group homes or sample a subset for performance.

issues.description: No error handling around parameter loading or runtime failures; main() does not validate inputs.
issues.solution: Add basic argument parsing, parameter validation, and try/except to emit clear error messages.
